prompt: Where does the planner put its `NavigationStack`?
hint: Once, at the root of what navigates.

choices.text: Around each screen that has a title
choices.why: Each would be a separate stack with its own path.

choices.text: Once, around the course list at the root
choices.why: Right: every screen pushed onto it gets the bar and a back button.

choices.text: In `PlannerApp`, around the `WindowGroup`
choices.why: A `WindowGroup` is a scene, and a stack is a view inside it.

choices.text: Inside every `NavigationLink`
choices.why: A link pushes onto a stack; it does not make one.

prompt: What can a stack built only from `NavigationLink(title) { DestinationView() }` not do?
hint: The stack knows only that some view was pushed.

choices.text: Show a back button on the pushed screen
choices.why: It shows one; that comes with any push.

choices.text: Push more than one screen in a row
choices.why: Links inside the destination push further.

choices.text: Be saved, or opened from a link
choices.why: Right: there is no value to save or to build a path from.

choices.text: Run on iOS 17
choices.why: It runs; it is the older form, not a removed one.

prompt: Why does `Route.course` carry the course's id rather than the `Course` itself?
hint: What would the detail screen show after a rename?

choices.text: It is looked up when shown, never a stale copy
choices.why: Right, and an id can be saved and read back.

choices.text: `Course` cannot be `Hashable`
choices.why: Lesson 1 made it `Hashable`.

choices.text: Enums may not hold structs as associated values
choices.why: They may; the reason is freshness, not a language rule.

choices.text: A string makes the push faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: Where should `navigationDestination(for: Route.self)` go?
hint: Apple's documentation warns about one kind of container.

choices.text: Inside each row of the `List`, next to its link
choices.why: That is a lazy container, which the documentation warns against.

choices.text: Inside the stack, on a view that is always there
choices.why: Right: on the root list, for instance.

choices.text: In `PlannerApp`, on the `WindowGroup`
choices.why: It has to be inside the stack it serves.

choices.text: Once per pushed screen, in its `body`
choices.why: One place decides the screen for a route.

prompt: `NavigationStack` compares the values on its path, so the value type must be ___.
hint: A protocol `Route` declares, besides `Codable` and `Sendable`.

prompt: Match each thing the person does to what happens to `model.path`.
hint: Section 04's table.

pairs.left: Saves a new session and returns to the list

prompt: With the SQL course's session `s3` on top, how many elements does `model.path` hold?
hint: The root is not in the path.

prompt: Why keep the path in `PlannerModel` rather than let `NavigationStack` keep it internally?
hint: Who else needs to change it?

choices.text: A stack that keeps its own path cannot push
choices.why: It pushes fine; links work either way.

choices.text: `NavigationPath` is deprecated
choices.why: It is current; it is for stacks of several value types.

choices.text: Notifications and links must put the app on a screen
choices.why: Right: with the path in hand, that is one assignment.

choices.text: So that every view can push without a `NavigationLink`
choices.why: Links still push; the model's path is for code outside the screens.

prompt: Why are `Route`'s associated values labelled, `course(id:)` rather than `course(String)`?
hint: Look at the saved JSON.

choices.text: Unlabelled associated values are not allowed in Swift 6
choices.why: They are allowed.

choices.text: The labels become the keys of the encoded JSON
choices.why: Right: `{"course":{"id":"sql"}}`.

choices.text: `Hashable` cannot be synthesised without labels
choices.why: It is synthesised either way.

choices.text: The navigation bar prints them as the title
choices.why: The title comes from `.navigationTitle`.

prompt: A saved path is `[.course(id: "sql"), .session(id: "s3")]` and `s3` was deleted since. What does `stillValid` give back?
hint: The longest start whose every route still names something.

choices.text: The whole path, and the session screen shows a message
choices.why: The point is not to push a screen for something that is gone.

choices.text: An empty path, back to the list
choices.why: The course still exists, so its screen is kept.

choices.text: `[.course(id: "sql")]`
choices.why: Right, as the program printed for `s3 deleted`.

choices.text: `[.session(id: "s3")]`, the screen on top
choices.why: That is the route that no longer names anything.

prompt: `stillValid` uses `prefix(while:)` and not `filter`. Which path shows why?
hint: A screen whose parent is gone.

choices.text: `[.week(day: "2026-10-19")]`, a single route
choices.why: With one route the two give the same answer.

choices.text: A course deleted, its session kept
choices.why: Right: `filter` would keep the session and push it with no course under it; `prefix(while:)` stops at the course and keeps neither.

choices.text: An empty path
choices.why: Both return it empty.

choices.text: A path where every route still exists
choices.why: Both return it whole.

prompt: After renaming the case `session` to `sessionDetail`, a path saved last week fails to decode. What should the app do?
hint: A saved path is saved data like any other.

choices.text: Crash, so the bug is noticed
choices.why: The person did nothing wrong; the app should carry on.

choices.text: Retry the decode until it works
choices.why: The same bytes fail the same way.

choices.text: Start at the root, with an empty path
choices.why: Right: losing a screen position is better than failing to open.

choices.text: Show the raw JSON so the person can fix it
choices.why: Nobody should be asked to edit a saved path.

prompt: Why does `planner://course/sql/session` get `nil`?
hint: Words are read in pairs.

choices.text: `session` is not a kind the planner has
choices.why: It is; `teacher` is the one it lacks.

choices.text: A word is left over: the link was cut short
choices.why: Right: `session` has no value after it.

choices.text: The host must be `planner`
choices.why: `planner` is the scheme; the host is `course`.

choices.text: Links may name only one route
choices.why: The first test's link names two.

prompt: `aLinkThatIsNotARouteIsRefused` ran once per argument. How many test cases did it report?
hint: Count the strings in `arguments:`.

prompt: Why is a deep link checked twice, by the parser and by `stillValid`?
hint: They check different things.

choices.text: The second catches parser bugs the tests missed
choices.why: It checks something the parser cannot know.

choices.text: One checks the URL's shape; the other, that its ids still exist
choices.why: Right: a well-formed link can name a session that was deleted.

choices.text: Apple requires two checks for custom schemes
choices.why: No such rule; it is the app's own design.

choices.text: The first runs on the device, the second on the server
choices.why: Both run in the app.

prompt: Why is adding a session a sheet and not a push?
hint: What should back do?

choices.text: A task that returns here
choices.why: Right: save or cancel, and the person is where they were.

choices.text: Forms cannot be pushed onto a `NavigationStack`
choices.why: They can; it would just be the wrong presentation.

choices.text: A sheet cannot be dismissed by accident
choices.why: A swipe dismisses one unless that is disabled.

choices.text: Sheets keep the new session even when cancelled
choices.why: Cancel throws the draft away.

prompt: The form inside the sheet has a `NavigationStack` of its own. Is that the nesting section 02 warned about?
hint: A sheet is a separate presentation.

choices.text: Yes, and the form should use the course screen's stack
choices.why: The sheet is not pushed onto that stack.

choices.text: No: it is a separate presentation
choices.why: Right: that is where *Cancel* and *Save* go.

choices.text: Yes, but SwiftUI merges the two stacks
choices.why: Nothing merges them.

choices.text: No, because sheets cannot contain a `NavigationStack`
choices.why: They can, which is what the form does.

prompt: Which presentation fits a study timer that marks the session done when the person stops it?
hint: It must not be lost to a swipe.

choices.text: A push onto the course's stack
choices.why: Back would abandon it, and it is not a place to return to.

choices.text: A sheet
choices.why: A swipe would end the timer without a decision.

choices.text: A full-screen cover
choices.why: Right: a mode the person ends on purpose, with its own Stop button.

choices.text: An alert
choices.why: An alert asks one question; a timer is a screen.
